correctness.rationale: For each edge I computed the minimum of two Hamming distances, packed the resulting distance signatures without collisions, and separately unioned the covered edges. The exact replay checks all required cardinalities against lower counts (resolving, covering, joint) (0,4,0), (0,16,0), (64,112,0), (1280,80,0) at d−1 and finds (4,32,176,160) joint sets at d. Monotonicity excludes all smaller subsets. The checks at d−2 establish ordinary minima 3 and 4 in dimensions 4 and 5. Full translation/coordinate-permutation orbits of the representative shapes give set equality, with sizes 4; 8 and 24; 16, 64 and 96; and 160. The repaired claim compares minimum cardinalities, not the possibility of augmenting every ordinary basis. Indeed, in Q5 only 160 of 1280 ordinary 4-bases are single deletions from an optimal joint set; {0,3,5,14} in binary-integer notation is a checked nonextendible ordinary basis. The complete replacement RESULT.md is under /workspace/repairs/5/. Replay: python3 /workspace/checks/5.py. No higher-dimensional conclusion follows from these tests.

value.rationale: Q4 and Q5 are successive standard cubes where adding a local coverage constraint provably changes the optimal size relative to pure edge identification. The complete basis geometry identifies exact placements, not merely a cheap extra case of a scalar table: three distinct four-dimensional orbits collapse to one rigid five-dimensional shape. This is a natural benchmark for the published joint parameter and for studying when and how an identification set can meet a local coverage constraint. It does not rest on the known Q2/Q3 minima or on a claim of arbitrary augmentation.
